22nov1602.summary: Henri IV asks the Landgrave for his promised advice on the coming Imperial diet, what to propose there for his allies, and whether to send his ambassador on to Saxony and Denmark.

12jan1603.summary: With the Emperor absent from the diet, the King expects nothing important there, notably no election of a King of the Romans; he complains that the duc de Bouillon wrote nothing of the Administrator of Strasbourg's visit.

27dec1604.summary: The King explains why he has not sent an embassy to the German princes (the Protestants' disunity and their support for Bouillon), reports the United Provinces' resolve to fight on, and his trouble with Spanish intrigues and the comte d'Auvergne.

28apr1605.summary: The passage Rommel regretted he could not decipher: the King's aid to the United Provinces and Geneva proves his care to maintain those of the reformed religion.

22dec1605.summary: After the Mérargues affair and the conspiracy in England the King urges the German princes to help the United Provinces with money and troops, promises to continue his own aid of two million livres, and asks what the Emperor intends at the diet.

20may1606.summary: The King's programme against the Spanish-Habsburg design on the Imperial diet: the kings and princes jealous of Spain should concert in defence of 'la liberté germanique'; the King of England's neutrality, Spinola's coming campaign and the weakness of the States.

24jan1609.summary: One line: the ministers of the Pope and the King of Spain will do all they can to reconcile Archduke Matthias with the Emperor.

system: Two-digit figures: bare = letters with up to four homophones, and comma, two-dot and overbar marks select three word/syllable/name lists, plus a dozen glyphs, a doubling sign and nulls.
